content.title: NEW PARENTS: DO THIS BEFORE YOU EVEN THINK ABOUT {{SLEEP}}
facts: **Lie down flat** for 10 minutes when the baby naps, even if you can't sleep — flat rest lowers your heart rate and resets your nervous system more than scrolling does.
**Eat standing up less** — sit down for at least one meal a day so your body actually registers you've eaten and digestion isn't rushed.
**Keep a water bottle at the changing station** — breastfeeding and sleep deprivation both spike your fluid needs, and dehydration makes exhaustion feel worse than it is.
**Ask for a 2-hour block, not 'help'** — vague offers rarely get used, but a scheduled 2-hour window actually gets protected and used for rest.
**Step outside for 5 minutes daily** — morning light exposure helps regulate your own circadian rhythm even when your sleep schedule is chaos.
**Lower the bar on dinner** — a 10-minute meal with protein beats skipping food until you crash and overeat at 9pm.
**Let one dish sit overnight** — protecting 15 minutes of rest matters more for your recovery than a spotless kitchen.
**Follow along** – for more daily health tips like this.

caption:
New parents, a few of these matter more than they sound. Lying down flat for just 10 minutes, even without falling asleep, lets your heart rate drop and your nervous system shift out of fight-or-flight mode — something scrolling on your phone never actually does. Getting outside for 5 minutes in the morning does more than you'd think too: natural light exposure early in the day helps anchor your circadian rhythm, which gets scrambled fast with newborn sleep patterns. And asking for a specific 2-hour block instead of a vague "let me know if you need anything" works because your brain and body need a guaranteed window to actually downshift into rest, not just a possibility of one.
